chapter: Tulsa bands, Trent, Holder and Kirk
title: The Gladewater and Longview oil-boom gig
summary: The band plays a ballroom between the two east Texas oil towns for a white manager, in mud and rain, with money borrowed from his brother.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So this guy, this job we were going down to Gladewater and Longview to play, and so we're going down there and this guy would give us a salary. I forget what it was, but they'd give us nice money, around ten dollars a man and that was big money. I think the fellow really meant well, but it rained, rained every night and you couldn't get there hardly for the mud, and it just was bad.
Was this a black guy or a white guy?
No, it was a white guy.

It was very fortunate, I started off, I didn't develop the idea of playing all the time of what I wanted to play. I played what the people wanted me to play, and so that made me do a lot of white work also, just as

much as I did, and through the years, that was proven even when I got to recording, and so anyway, this guy got a nickel too, this kind of manager, and I had borrowed money to come down there, I had borrowed some money from my brother, who was teaching, and I borrowed some money from him, I had this job.
Those were two oil boom towns, and the ballroom was just in between them. I think we lived in Longview.
